entries.title: The Chrome extension is offered where it helps
entries.body: When a page will not import for a reason the Chrome extension can get round, the add page now offers the extension underneath the failure, on a computer with a mouse or trackpad. The Help page's section on adding an article describes it, with a link to install it, and typing "extension" or "chrome" in the command bar opens those instructions. The extension adds the page as your browser shows it.

entries.title: More cited works get a web note
entries.body: In the Sources bibliography, cited works in your own articles can get a web note from more kinds of search result, including works with no identifier if the article came from a web address. A note from a page that may not be the work's own says so, and still quotes its evidence. Searches that found nothing can be retried.

entries.title: Executive summaries fold like the abstract
entries.body: An opening section labelled Executive summary, Key points, Highlights, Research highlights, Significance, Significance statement or Author summary now folds into its own short stub, named by its label, and keeps its row in Structure. Articles added earlier get these folds only when the app processes them again.

entries.title: Structure flickers less and uses its full width
entries.body: The Structure panel's list no longer leaves an empty gap down its right-hand side. As you scroll, the panel follows your place less often, so it no longer redraws at every section you pass or when the bottom bar slides away and back. When you are reading an article someone has shared with you, the bar at the top now stays put while Structure is open.

entries.title: Cited by works for more arXiv papers
entries.body: For some arXiv papers added from their arxiv.org address, the Cited by list in Sources showed nothing, because the record of the paper carried a different title. It now accepts that record when the paper's address and two of its authors match.

entries.title: Review pages are not mistaken for cited works
entries.body: A search result whose title ended in a separate word "Reviews" could be taken for a cited work when the app checked titles. It is turned away now, while journal names such as Reviews of Modern Physics are still accepted.
